prompt.title: Look back from the end
prompt.text: Picture a moment far ahead: the end of your life, a last year, a big anniversary, your final day at work. Write what you'd want to be true then. The values you hear go into your mission.
prompt.glossText: This is the habit's own idea: begin with the end in mind. Know where you want to arrive before you set off.
prompt.whyItMatters: Day to day, the loud things win. Looking back from the far end quiets them and shows what you'd actually regret missing. Ten minutes here can change what you plan for years.
prompt.chapterReference: Habit 2: Begin with the End in Mind

list.empty: Nothing here yet. Start with your funeral; it's the one that changes most.

funeral.title: Your funeral
funeral.text: Three years from now. Four people speak about you: family, a friend, someone from work, someone from your community.

oneYear.title: One year left
oneYear.text: You've just learned you have one healthy year. Nothing else changes.

anniversary.title: A milestone anniversary
anniversary.text: A big anniversary of a relationship that matters: a marriage, a friendship, a partnership. Friends are raising a glass.

lastDay.title: Your last day at work
lastDay.text: You're leaving for good. People gather to say what your work meant.

family.label: What they say
family.prompt: Someone from your family stands up. What do you want them to say about who you were to them?
family.placeholder: e.g. He was home for dinner. He listened, even when he was tired.

friend.label: What they say
friend.prompt: A friend speaks next. What kind of friend do you want to have been?
friend.placeholder: e.g. The one you could call at 2 a.m. and he'd come.

work.label: What they say
work.prompt: Someone from work. What do you want them to remember about working with you?
work.placeholder: e.g. She made the juniors better and gave them the credit.

community.label: What they say
community.prompt: Someone from your neighbourhood, place of worship or club. What did you give there?
community.placeholder: e.g. He showed up. Every clean-up, every funeral, every fundraiser.

who.label: Who would you spend it with
who.prompt: Who would you spend the year with, and how?
who.placeholder: e.g. My kids and my mother. Long meals, no phones.

stop.label: Stop doing
stop.prompt: What would you stop doing straight away?
stop.placeholder: e.g. Saying yes to meetings I don't need to be in.

finish.label: Start or finish
finish.prompt: What would you start, or finish, while you still can?
finish.placeholder: e.g. Write down the family stories before they're gone.

which.label: Whose anniversary
which.prompt: Whose anniversary is it, and how many years?

built.label: What you built
built.prompt: What do you hope the two of you will have built by then?
built.placeholder: e.g. A home people want to come back to. Still laughing at the same jokes.

said.label: What they say
said.prompt: What would the people there say about how you treat each other?
said.placeholder: e.g. They still ask each other first.

contributed.label: What you contributed
contributed.prompt: What do you want to have contributed, in your work and beyond it?
contributed.placeholder: e.g. Two products people still use. A team that runs without me.

next.label: What you'll do next
next.prompt: What will you do with your time once you've left?
next.placeholder: e.g. Teach two mornings a week. Fix the boat.

valuesPrompt: What does this tell you you value? One or two words each.

readBack.reflectionPrompt: Read your answers once more. What surprises you, or keeps coming up?
readBack.reflectionPlaceholder: e.g. Nobody mentioned my title. Everyone mentioned time.

checklist.value: Write down at least one value you heard

guide.inShort: You'll pick a far-off moment and write what you'd want to be true then, in a few lines per prompt. After each answer you'll name the value behind it. Ten to fifteen minutes per long view; start with the funeral.
howTo: Tap "New long view" and pick a scene. The funeral first, if you can.
Read the prompt slowly. Write what you'd want to hear, not what you expect.
Under each answer, add one or two words for the value behind it.
On the last step, read it all back and note what stands out.
Come back another day for the next scene. The values pile up in the summary.
Tap "Mark done" after one complete long view. Do the others when you're ready for your mission.

fields.label: What they say
fields.value: The one you could call at 2 a.m. and he'd come.

fields.label: Who would you spend it with

guide.afterwards: Take the summary's values into Your mission; they're the first step there. If a value showed up in three views, it belongs in the first line. Redo a long view in a year and compare.
